I want silicon that
behaves like biology.

Biotechnologist by training, self-taught in ML, born in Kolkata to a nuclear physicist. Agent infrastructure, tissue classifiers, embodied software — a gate that can fail and a number that can be read on every one.

field
notes

origins — kolkata, 1999Born to a nuclear physicist and a teacher. Ramakrishna Mission, Bengali medium, where only the minimum mattered. Wanted medicine, came out a biotechnologist (VIT Vellore) — then taught myself the ML half, because I wanted silicon to behave like the cells I was studying.
habitat — the day jobAgent infrastructure for a 500-person org: routing, budgets, failure isolation, token cost down 15×. Every quarter I find the repeated work and build software factories around it — the system builds itself, I monitor.
nocturnal — the nightsTissue classifiers, motion rigs that walk without limping, software with a voice and a body. One question underneath: how far can silicon go before it counts as biology?
observed behaviour — morningsWake 5:30. Stretch stiff tendons. Swim at the local club. Cook the day's food, then cook more code than food. Cyclist. Jungle-walker. 3D-print what I design. Papers and comics, both.

HISTOGATE · STAIN-INVARIANT TISSUE CLASSIFIER · SHIPPED

It declines tissue it doesn't recognize.

A 9-class colorectal H&E classifier. First version: 97% on its own data, 78% on a hospital it never saw — the stain problem. Fixed with Beer–Lambert absorbance physics in training, a k-NN familiarity gate, conformal sets on top. Served live from my own GPU; three failed training runs published in the repo.
